script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Sports
Theme: small-town life

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

INT. HIGH SCHOOL GYM - EARLY MORNING

A lone figure, JAMES, in his late twenties, moves with quiet determination. He wears a faded blue t-shirt, sweatpants, and running shoes. The GYM is dimly lit, the echo of his footsteps bouncing off the empty bleachers.

JAMES (V.O.)
I'm back.

EXT. SMALL-TOWN STREETS - DAY

James, wearing a backpack, jogs through the quaint, bustling small town. He exchanges warm greetings with townsfolk.

INT. COUNTY FAIRGROUNDS - AFTERNOON

James walks into the large, empty FAIRGROUNDS. The sun sets behind him, illuminating a dilapidated sign that reads "BASEBALL FIELD."

JAMES (V.O.)
Home.

INT. JAMES'S LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

James sits on an old couch, surrounded by photos of baseball teams from his past. He clutches a newspaper, reading the headline: "Local Baseball Team Dissolved Due to Lack of Funding."

JAMES (V.O.)
I can't let them down.

EXT. HIGH SCHOOL - DAY

James enters the school, talking with PRINCIPAL LUCAS.

PRINCIPAL LUCAS
(smiling)
I've heard the rumors. You've got quite the reputation.

JAMES
(smiling back)
Thank you, sir.

PRINCIPAL LUCAS
I want to help. The school board has allocated a small budget for a new team. Can you make it work?

JAMES
Absolutely.

EXT. HIGH SCHOOL GYM - DAY

James gathers a group of teenagers, most of whom have never played baseball before. He encourages them, despite their initial skepticism.

JAMES
We've got a shot at something special here. You just need to believe.

EXT. PRACTICE FIELD - DAY

The team practices together, with James teaching them the basics. They laugh, sweat, and grow as a team.

INT. JAMES'S LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

James works tirelessly to find sponsors and resources for the team. He writes letters, makes phone calls, and searches online.

JAMES (V.O.)
It's going to be tough, but we're going to make it work.

EXT. LOCAL SPORTS STORE - DAY

James enters the store, talking with OWNER MRS. JONES.

MRS. JONES
You've got some spirit, James. I might be able to help out.

INT. HIGH SCHOOL GYM - EVENING

The team practices, their skills improving with each passing day. They celebrate small victories together.

INT. JAMES'S LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

James receives a letter from a local business, agreeing to sponsor the team. He reads the news aloud, eliciting cheers from the team members gathered around.

JAMES (V.O.)
We're going to make it, guys. We're going to make it.

EXT. COMMUNITY PARK - DAY

The team plays their first game against a rival town. Despite early setbacks, they rally together, with James leading the charge. They win, much to the delight of the small-town crowd.

INT. HIGH SCHOOL GYM - NIGHT

The team gathers for a celebration, their morale high. They share stories of their journey and look forward to the future.

JAMES
(raising a cup)
To us. To small-town life. To believing.

FADE OUT.
